daily_reality.summary: MRI technologists operate MRI scanners to produce diagnostic images of patients' internal structures. They work in hospitals, imaging centers, and outpatient facilities. Standard 40-hour week with on-call for emergency imaging. Patient positioning, safety screening, and image quality are core responsibilities.
typical_tasks: Screening patients for MRI safety: metal implants, pacemakers, claustrophobia
Positioning patients correctly within the MRI scanner
Selecting and programming appropriate MRI sequences for the ordered study
Administering contrast agents (gadolinium) via IV when ordered
Monitoring patients during scans for comfort and safety
Reviewing images for quality and diagnostic adequacy
Sending images to PACS for radiologist interpretation
Maintaining MRI equipment and performing quality control checks
Documenting procedures and patient information in EHR
Communicating with radiologists about image findings and protocols

deadlines.routine_scan: 30-90 minutes per exam depending on body part
deadlines.image_delivery: Images to PACS within minutes of completion
deadlines.equipment_qc: Daily/weekly per ACR and manufacturer guidelines

daily_reality.seasonality: No significant seasonality. Emergency MRI year-round. Elective scans may slow during holiday periods.

regulatory.summary: ARRT certification is the primary credential (MR specialty). Some states require licensure. ACR accreditation governs MRI facility quality standards. Strict MRI safety protocols due to powerful magnetic fields.

key_laws.description: Many states require licensure for MRI technologists; requirements vary

key_laws.description: American College of Radiology quality standards for MRI facilities

key_laws.name: ACR Guidance Document on MR Safe Practices

requirements: Associate's or bachelor's degree in radiologic technology or MRI technology
ARRT certification in Radiography (R) and/or MRI (MR)
ARMRIT (American Registry of Magnetic Resonance Imaging Technologists) certification alternative
24 CE credits biennially for ARRT renewal

regulatory.recent_changes: Growing emphasis on MRI safety culture. New gadolinium retention research impacting contrast protocols. 7T MRI systems entering clinical use. AI-assisted MRI reconstruction reducing scan times.

pain_points: Claustrophobic and anxious patients delaying scans
Keeping up with rapidly evolving MRI technology

terminology.summary: MRI-specific physics and medical imaging terminology. Highly technical vocabulary combining electromagnetics, anatomy, and radiology.

terms.Tesla (T): Unit of magnetic field strength (1.5T, 3T, 7T scanners)
terms.T1-weighted: MRI sequence emphasizing fat (bright) and fluid (dark)
terms.FLAIR: Fluid-Attenuated Inversion Recovery — suppresses CSF signal
terms.contrast: Gadolinium-based agent injected IV to enhance visualization
terms.artifact: Unwanted distortion in MRI image (motion, metal, aliasing)
terms.FOV: Field of View — area of anatomy covered by the scan
terms.coil: RF antenna placed on body part to detect MRI signal
terms.quench: Emergency shutdown of MRI magnet (releases cryogen)
terms.ferromagnetic: Material attracted by magnetic field — dangerous in MRI zone
terms.Zone IV: ACR designation for the MRI scan room (highest restriction)
terms.SAR: Specific Absorption Rate — RF energy deposited in patient tissue
terms.MRA: Magnetic Resonance Angiography — imaging blood vessels

career_psychology.summary: Well-compensated imaging career (median $88,180). 7.1% growth projected. Requires strong technical and patient care skills. MRI safety expertise is a differentiator. Multiple advancement paths.
career_path: Associate's or bachelor's degree in radiologic/MRI technology
Experienced MRI tech with multi-system proficiency
MRI applications specialist for equipment manufacturer
fears: MRI safety incident (ferromagnetic projectile, patient with unreported implant)
Keeping up with rapidly changing MRI technology
motivation: Constant technology evolution keeps work interesting
burnout_factors: Repetitive scanning of similar body parts
Difficult patients (claustrophobia, inability to hold still)

community.summary: Professional community through ARRT, SMRT (Section for MRI Technologists within ISMRM), and ASRT. Manufacturer-specific training communities also important.

associations.name: American Society of Radiologic Technologists (ASRT)
associations.type: Professional membership society for radiologic technologists

online_communities.name: MRI technologist Facebook groups
online_communities.description: Multiple active groups for MRI professionals

events: RSNA Annual Meeting (Radiological Society of North America)
ASRT Annual Governance and House of Delegates

market.summary: Growing field with 7.1% projected growth (2024-2034). ~3,100 new jobs expected. Driven by aging population, expanding clinical applications, and preference for non-ionizing imaging. AI not replacing MRI techs but enhancing capabilities.

demand_forecast.driver: Aging population, expanded clinical MRI applications

market_trends: AI-assisted image reconstruction reducing scan times
7T MRI entering clinical practice for neuroimaging
Point-of-care and portable MRI (Hyperfine) expanding access
Growing demand for cardiac MRI specialists
MRI-guided interventional procedures creating new hybrid roles
